def: Reading real traces, naming what went wrong and counting failure kinds so that fixes are chosen by evidence.
The full record of one request: input, prompts, model and tool calls, retrieved documents and final output, in order.
A first review pass in which the reviewer writes a short free-text note about each trace, without preset categories.
A second pass that groups open-coding notes into named categories and counts them.
A short list of named failure categories, ideally mutually exclusive on the first failure, with counts.
The earliest wrong step in a trace, which is counted because later errors often follow from it.
The point at which new traces stop revealing new failure kinds or changing existing categories.
The tendency for people's grading criteria to change as they read outputs, because grading helps define the criteria.
